messages.text: Norris beats Antonelli to victory in Dutch GP

metadata.summary: Lando Norris outduelled championship leader Kimi Antonelli to claim his second successive race victory by winning the Dutch Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Dutch GP: Lando Norris beats Kimi Antonelli to victory in Zandvoort to claim second successive race win | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Breaking Dutch GP: Lando Norris beats Kimi Antonelli to victory in Zandvoort to claim second successive race win Lando Norris wins Dutch Grand Prix to secure back-to-back victories; Kimi Antonelli extends overall championship lead to 59 points by finishing second; Norris reduces title-race deficit to 83 points; George Russell holds off Lewis Hamilton for third; Max Verstappen crashed out on first lap Sunday 23 August 2026 16:24, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris hunted down Kimi Antonelli and Lewis Hamilton to take the race lead at the Dutch Grand Prix Lando Norris outduelled championship leader Kimi Antonelli to claim his second successive race victory by winning the Dutch Grand Prix. McLaren's Norris started on pole in Zandvoort but lost the lead to Antonelli at an early standing restart after Red Bull's Max Verstappen triggered a red flag at his home race by crashing out at the end of the first lap. After struggling to pressure Antonelli on the first stint, Norris was far quicker after switching onto a hard tyre at the first round of pit stops, and eventually passed the Mercedes after emerging from his second stop with far fresher tyres than the Italian. metadata.summary: Diamond Necklace tasted defeat for the first time as Aventure served up a reminder of her top-class credentials in the Sumbe Prix Jean et Louis Romanet at Deauville.
metadata.content: Deauville: Aventure ends Diamond Necklace's unbeaten record with Sumbe Prix Jean et Louis Romanet win | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to content Deauville: Aventure ends Diamond Necklace's unbeaten record with Sumbe Prix Jean et Louis Romanet win Aventure produced an upset in the Sumbe Prix Jean et Louis Romanet, defeating the previously-unbeaten Diamond Necklace in the Deauville Group One; also on the card, Senorita Bonita dazzled for the Simon and Ed Crisford team in the Prix Morny Sunday 23 August 2026 16:09, UK Image: Aventure claimed the honours at Deauville (photo:Zuzanna Lupa) Diamond Necklace tasted defeat for the first time as Aventure served up a reminder of her top-class credentials in the Sumbe Prix Jean et Louis Romanet at Deauville. Aidan O'Brien's daughter of St Mark's Basilica was expected to dazzle once again in France, as she had done when landing the Prix Marcel Boussac, Poule d'Essai Des Pouliches and Prix de Diane on her travels during what was an unbeaten six-race career to date. However, she had no answer to the experience of her Christophe Ferland-trained elder, who added to last year's Group One strike in the Prix Vermeille and earned herself a quote of 20/1 for another crack at the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe from bookmakers, a race in which she finished second to Bluestocking in 2024. messages.text: ECB investigating as Carse handcuffed by police outside Derby nightclub

metadata.summary: The ECB is investigating an incident involving England player Brydon Carse, after footage emerged showing the bowler handcuffed by police outside a Derby nightclub on Saturday night.
metadata.content: Brydon Carse: ECB investigating after England seamer handcuffed by police outside Derby nightclub | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to content Breaking Brydon Carse: ECB investigating after England seamer handcuffed by police outside Derby nightclub England fast bowler Brydon Carse seen in handcuffs outside nightclub in Derby in video circulating on social media; Carse set to be in England squad for second Pakistan Test starting on Thursday at Lord's Sunday 23 August 2026 16:39, UK Image: Brydon Carse was seen in handcuffs outside a nightclub in Derby The ECB is investigating an incident involving England player Brydon Carse, after footage emerged showing the bowler handcuffed by police outside a Derby nightclub on Saturday night. In a statement to Sky Sports News , the ECB confirmed is it aware of the incident. A video obtained by The Telegraph shows Carse with police, with a Durham team-mate talking to him. Former England captain Ben Stokes is also pictured. According to The Telegraph, Carse was briefly detained by police but not arrested. He returned to the team hotel soon after and it is unclear what led the police placing him in handcuffs. Carse was part of England's squad for the first Test against Pakistan at Headingley but was not in the starting XI, so was released to play for his county.
